column3: NASB sets the title in braces before verse 1 and transliterates “a poem” as “A Maskil.” Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “to be.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Lift up Your footsteps” is rendered “Turn Your footsteps.”
Close to the Hebrew; “their signs as signs” is rendered “their own standards for signs.”
The Hebrew is obscure; NASB renders “It seems as if one had lifted up His axe in a forest of trees.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “axes and crowbars” is rendered “hatchet and hammers.”
Close to the Hebrew; “let us oppress them” is rendered “Let us completely subdue them.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “them.”
“To a people, to desert-dwellers” is rendered “for the creatures of the wilderness.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a luminary” is rendered “the light.”
